sections.content: If you're searching for real estate deals in Shreveport LA, you've landed on a market that most coastal investors are still sleeping on. Shreveport sits in the northwest corner of Louisiana, right on the Texas border, and it's quietly offering some of the best cash-on-cash returns in the entire South. With median home prices well below the national average and a steady rental demand driven by healthcare, energy, and military sectors, this market deserves a serious look. Whether you're brand new to investing or a seasoned wholesaler looking to expand your portfolio, this guide will walk you through everything you need to know. If you're just getting started, check out our full Real Estate Investing for Beginners guide before diving in.
Shreveport Real Estate Market Overview

Shreveport is Louisiana's third-largest city with a population of around 185,000 people. The greater Shreveport-Bossier City metro area pushes that number closer to 440,000. The city's economy is anchored by Barksdale Air Force Base, Willis-Knighton Health System, and a growing film production industry — often called the 'Hollywood South' pipeline. These diverse employment drivers keep rental demand relatively stable, even during national downturns. Unlike hot markets like Austin or Nashville, Shreveport hasn't experienced dramatic price run-ups, which means investors can still find deeply discounted properties without competing in 30-offer bidding wars.
Average Home Prices in Shreveport

As of 2024, the median home price in Shreveport sits around $145,000 to $160,000, compared to the national median of approximately $420,000. That gap is everything for investors focused on cash flow and equity. Distressed properties — the kind wholesalers and flippers target — regularly trade between $30,000 and $90,000, giving investors a wide margin to work with. Rent rates for a typical 3-bedroom home run between $900 and $1,300 per month, which produces strong rent-to-price ratios that easily meet the classic 1% rule in many neighborhoods. For context, a $70,000 rental property generating $900 per month hits a 1.28% rent-to-price ratio — numbers that are nearly impossible to find in major metros.

Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Shreveport

Not every zip code in Shreveport is investor-friendly, so knowing where to focus is critical. The city has a mix of strong cash flow areas, emerging neighborhoods with appreciation potential, and zones you should avoid until you know the market well.
Top Investor Neighborhoods to Target

items: South Highlands / Line Avenue Corridor — A historic area with solid owner-occupant demand and good flip potential. Homes here often sell between $120,000 and $220,000 after renovation.

Bossier City (across the Red River) — Technically a separate city, but considered part of the Shreveport metro. Strong rental demand from Barksdale AFB military families. Median prices run $160,000 to $200,000.
Queensborough — A working-class neighborhood with low entry prices ($40,000–$80,000) and consistent rental demand. Great for buy-and-hold investors targeting long-term cash flow.
Broadmoor — An up-and-coming area near medical corridors with a mix of renovation opportunities and newer construction. Prices are rising steadily.
Western Hills — Suburban feel with good school ratings, attracting families. Solid for Section 8 rentals and long-term holds.
Allendale — A distressed area with the lowest entry prices in the city. High-risk but high-reward for experienced investors with strong contractor networks.

Wholesale Deals

Wholesaling is extremely active in Shreveport because of the large volume of distressed and vacant properties throughout the city. Many sellers are motivated — dealing with probate situations, tax delinquency, or inherited homes they don't want to manage from out of state. A skilled wholesaler can routinely put properties under contract for $25,000 to $55,000 and assign them to cash buyers for assignment fees ranging from $5,000 to $20,000. The key is building a reliable cash buyer list of local flippers and landlords who close fast. To learn the mechanics, read our guide on Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners before you start making offers.
Fix and Flip Opportunities

Shreveport's fix and flip market rewards investors who understand local renovation costs. Labor is significantly cheaper here than in coastal cities — a full gut rehab that might cost $80,000 in Los Angeles can often be done for $35,000 to $50,000 in Shreveport. Profitable flips typically follow this formula: buy at 65%–70% of ARV minus repairs. For example, a home with a $150,000 ARV and $40,000 in rehab costs should be purchased for no more than $57,500 to maintain healthy margins. Focus on neighborhoods like South Highlands and Broadmoor where buyer demand supports higher post-renovation sale prices.
Buy-and-Hold Rental Properties

Long-term rentals are where many out-of-state investors build serious wealth in Shreveport. The low purchase prices combined with reasonable rent rates create cash flow that simply doesn't exist in expensive markets. Military families near Barksdale AFB, healthcare workers, and university students all create diverse rental demand. Many investors are also finding success with Section 8 housing vouchers, which guarantee government-backed rent payments and reduce vacancy risk. A properly managed 3-bedroom home purchased for $65,000 with a $950 monthly rent can generate $400 to $600 in monthly cash flow after all expenses — a 7%–10% cash-on-cash return.
Shreveport Market Trends to Watch in 2024

items: Film industry growth: Louisiana's generous film tax credits continue attracting productions, bringing well-paid temporary workers who need short-term rentals and furnished housing.
Population stability: While Shreveport has faced slight population declines, the metro area remains stable thanks to military and healthcare employment anchors.

Rising insurance costs: Louisiana insurance rates have climbed sharply. Factor this into your cash flow projections — budget $2,500 to $4,500 annually for homeowner's insurance on investment properties.
Increased investor competition: Out-of-state investors are slowly discovering the market. Off-market deals are becoming more important as listed inventory gets picked over quickly.
Infrastructure investment: The city is actively investing in economic development initiatives that could spur appreciation in targeted zones over the next 5–10 years.

Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Shreveport
Investing remotely in a market like Shreveport is very doable, but it requires building the right local team before you commit capital. Here's how to approach it strategically.

items: Find a local property manager first: Before buying anything, identify a trusted property management company familiar with Shreveport neighborhoods. Expect management fees of 8%–10% of monthly rent.
Build a reliable contractor network: Get at least 3 contractor bids on any property before closing. Renovation cost estimates from afar are notoriously inaccurate without local intel.

Use off-market deal sourcing: Most of the best deals never hit the MLS. Read our guide on How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals to learn direct mail, driving for dollars, and other proven sourcing methods.

Understand Louisiana-specific laws: Louisiana uses a civil law system based on the Napoleonic Code, which affects property law differently than common law states. Work with a local real estate attorney for closings.

Visit at least once before committing large capital: A single trip to walk neighborhoods and meet your team will save you from expensive mistakes. Book a 3-day scouting trip before deploying serious money.
Analyze every deal rigorously: Don't rely on gut instinct. Use tools like our How to Analyze Real Estate Deals Like a Pro framework to evaluate every opportunity with consistent criteria.
Track local market data: Bookmark our dedicated Shreveport LA market page for updated deal flow, median prices, and investor activity data.

sections.content: When evaluating Shreveport rentals, always budget for higher-than-average vacancy (plan for 10%–15%) and factor in Louisiana's elevated insurance costs. A deal that looks great on paper can underperform if you underestimate these two expenses.
Is Shreveport Right for Your Investment Strategy?

Shreveport isn't a market for investors chasing rapid appreciation or luxury flips. It's a market for investors who want strong cash flow, low entry prices, and deals that pencil out without creative financing gymnastics. If your goal is to build a portfolio of cash-flowing rentals, find wholesale deals with healthy assignment fees, or execute affordable flips with wide margins, Shreveport deserves serious attention. The investors who get in now — before national media discovers this market — will look very smart in five years.
